# Agent environments

## What an environment is
State, observations, actions, dynamics. The reward is a separate claim about what matters.

## Partial observability (POMDP)
When the agent cannot see the full state it must maintain a belief and sometimes act to gather information. Measurement can be an action with a cost.

## Attention as a hidden variable
Learners do not read everything shown to them. Attention gates learning and drains with fatigue.

# Evaluating agents

## pass@k vs pass^k
pass@k: any of k runs succeeds. pass^k: all k succeed. Reliability is what deployment needs.

## Proxy vs direct measures
A quiz score is a proxy. Retention a week later is closer to the thing itself.

args.text:
## Draft scaffold to revise

### Environment definition
Environment = the student-at-computer study setting.
- **State:** underlying student/task state, including current knowledge, attention/fatigue, course materials, notes, calendar, and pending messages.
- **Observations:** what the assistant can observe through tools, such as assignment text, notes, calendar events, messages, quiz scores, and visible files/readings. This is only a partial view of the full state.
- **Actions:** reading/assigning sections, sending explanations or hints, quizzing, editing notes, scheduling study blocks, checking course pages/messages, waiting, and ending the session.
- **Dynamics:** the student learns from readings, messages, and quizzes; attention changes over time; time passes during activities; memory can improve with practice and decay with delay; new messages/events can appear.
- **Why partial observability matters:** the assistant cannot directly observe true understanding or attention, so it must infer them from behavior such as replies and quiz performance.

### Evaluation
Use **pass^k**, not pass@k.
- **pass@k:** at least one of k runs succeeds.
- **pass^k:** all k runs succeed.
- **Why pass^k here:** the build is about reliability across runs/seeds, not just getting lucky once.

Report pass^k on at least 3 seeds by defining a success criterion, running the agent multiple times per seed, and marking a seed as passing only if all k runs on that seed succeed.

args.text:
### Paste-ready revision

## What I built
I built a study-assistant agent for the student-at-computer setting. The agent can inspect course materials and notes, message the student, assign short readings, run quizzes, and update the write-up. Its goal is to help the student prepare for the Friday build within a limited session.

## Environment definition
The environment is the student-at-computer study setting. The **state** includes the student’s underlying knowledge, attention/fatigue, current task status, notes, files, calendar, and messages. The assistant does not observe this full state directly. Instead, it receives **observations** through tools such as assignment text, files, notes, calendar events, messages, reading activity, and quiz scores. This makes the problem **partially observable**.

The assistant’s **actions** include opening or assigning readings, sending explanations or hints, answering directly, running quizzes, editing notes, checking course pages/messages, scheduling study blocks, waiting, and ending the session. The **dynamics** are that the student may learn from readings, explanations, and quizzes; attention changes over time; and time passes as actions are taken. Inference is required because true understanding and attention are hidden, so the agent must estimate them from behavior such as responses and quiz performance.

## Evaluation
We evaluate with **pass^k** on at least 3 seeds. Here, **pass@k** means that at least one of k runs succeeds, while **pass^k** means that all k runs succeed. We use pass^k because it measures reliability across repeated runs rather than whether the agent succeeds once by luck. A seed is counted as passing only if every run for that seed succeeds under the chosen success criterion.
